item.title: ThermLeT: Transformer-based Temperature Prediction for 2.5D Chiplet Architecture
item.description:
Authors: Varun Darshana Parekh, Anusha Devulapally, Sivani Devarapalli, Cassius Henderson, Shimeng Yu, Vijaykrishnan Narayanan

The drive toward heterogeneous 2.5D chiplet packages promises unmatched performance and customization, yet the resulting density amplifies thermal challenges. To facilitate rapid design space exploration, we present ThermLeT, a multimodal transformer-based, scale invariant surrogate that integrates power density maps, spatial coordinate embeddings, material properties and heat transfer rate to predict steady state temperature in 13 ms, about four orders of magnitude faster than conventional finite element solvers such as ANSYS. item.title: Sparse Integer Fourier Transform and Its Application In Machine Learning
item.description:
Authors: Jinyang Li, Jie Chen

item.description:
Authors: Alexey Ignatiev, Peter J. Stuckey, Joao Marques-Silva

item.title: EvoDisco: Strategy Discovery for Evolving Agent Memory
item.description:
Authors: Mingyang Liu, Qingcan Kang, Shixiong Kai, Kaichao Liang, Xiaojin Fu, Tao Zhong, Linqi Song

Large language model agents accumulate experience in memory, and how that memory evolves during interaction is as important as what it stores. Recent methods update memory online, yet both the operators that transform memory and the rules that select them remain fixed by design. We propose EvoDisco, which formulates agent memory evolution as evolutionary strategy discovery: the agent must discover which operator to apply, when to apply it, and how to instantiate it, rather than rewriting memory under a static operator schedule

item.title: TempQuant: Learning Adaptive Temperatures for Quantized Language Models
item.description:
Authors: Mukund Athmaram, Liang Ma, Manoj Rao

Large language models are increasingly deployed at low precision, yet quantization can degrade their performance. We study how quantization interacts with decoding settings such as the sampling temperature and top-p by examining how it distorts the model's next-token probabilities. Measuring entropy during generation across deployed temperatures, we find that quantization warms the model on average, and that temperature matters much more for the performance of a quantized model than for its full-precision counterpart

item.title: EgoHandWAM: Probing the Role of Hand Motion in Egocentric World Action Modeling
item.description:
Authors: Kailin Wang, Haoxiang Jie, Yaoyuan Yan, Zhiyou Heng, Zhaosong Li

How much does hand motion tell us about what a first-person camera will see next? EgoHandWAM forecasts three-dimensional wrist and fingertip trajectories and a future visual feature from the current image and recent hand states. We train on 751,065 EgoDex windows using a frozen DINOv2 encoder. On held-out development sessions, the action-only model reduces two-second wrist endpoint error from 60.26 to 56.48~mm relative to a stationary forecast
